fact_check.claim: 2025-26 Cornell budget: housing $13,744, food $7,604, books $1,234, personal $2,182, transportation 'Varies'; 2026-27 heading has no figures
fact_check.note: Page lists exactly these 2025-26 figures (transportation 'Varies by region'); 2026-27 figures did not come through. Sum $24,764 and monthly divisions (1,527 / 1,145 / 845 / 137 / 242) check out arithmetically.

fact_check.claim: The estimate leaves out premium on-campus or off-campus housing options
fact_check.note: Page says cost of attendance excludes fees not charged to all students, such as 'premium on-campus or off-campus housing options'.

fact_check.claim: Off-campus: look for housing that costs less for 12 months than the off-campus housing and dining budget; need calculated the same way; aid cannot cover security deposit, first and last month's rent, or rent in months not a registered student
fact_check.note: All three statements appear on the page. Page says 'not enrolled as a student'; article's 'registered' is a close paraphrase.

fact_check.claim: $13,744 housing line equals two semesters of the $6,872 residence hall double for 2026-27
fact_check.note: Page: $6,872 per semester for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027, $13,744 for the academic year. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Residence hall rate covers gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet up to 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Quoted on page. 'Meal plan required' claim was removed, as asked.

fact_check.claim: Collegetown houses about $800 to $1,300 per person a month; lowest 2-3 bedroom apartment about $1,300; house rents roughly on par with on-campus housing
fact_check.note: All match the Sept. 2, 2025 column.

fact_check.claim: Higher-end apartments about $1,450 for a 3-4 bedroom up to $2,300 for a studio
fact_check.note: Column: higher-end 3- or 4-bedroom about $1,450, studio up to $2,300.

fact_check.claim: Column author is 'a Cornell Daily Sun columnist (ILR, Class of 2027)'
fact_check.note: The fetched page confirms a Sun columnist and the September 2025 date; the school and class year were not in the text returned. Not a figure; low risk.

fact_check.claim: Column mentions kitchen appliances and cleaning supplies as furnishing costs, no prices
fact_check.note: Column mentions furnishing a first apartment with appliances and cleaning supplies adds up quickly; no prices given.

fact_check.claim: RentCafe Collegetown (updated Oct 30, 2026): studio $2,006, 1-bed $2,342, 2-bed $3,414, all rentals $2,815, down 2.59% from $2,890
fact_check.note: All figures and the update date match.

fact_check.claim: A $3,414 two-bedroom split two ways is $1,707 each
fact_check.note: Arithmetic correct and labeled as ours.

fact_check.claim: 'If you are' bullet: a $1,707 share puts you near $2,420 with utilities and phone
fact_check.note: Article's own arithmetic: 1,707 + 330 + 137 + 242 = 2,416 before utilities and phone (and before the bus pass). Adding the table's utilities and phone ($105 to $205) gives about $2,520 to $2,620. The $2,420 figure omits utilities and phone, contradicting the bullet's wording.

fact_check.claim: Table: subtotal $1,500-$2,030; with utilities and phone $1,600-$2,240; apartment totals $2,150-$3,030 before utilities and $2,260-$3,240 with
Nguyen 2022 Sun column: listed prices often reflect cost per person rather than per unit
fact_check.note: Column describes his search where listings over $1,000 were per person, not per unit. It is his experience and does not claim this is common, so 'often' is slightly broader than the source; this wording was the one the previous review requested.

fact_check.claim: Nguyen signed junior-year lease in October of sophomore year; students sign well before move-in
fact_check.note: Column: signed first lease in October, 10 months before moving in; students sign sometimes over a year ahead.

fact_check.claim: OmniRide passes cost $200 a year, pro-rated monthly, current rate shown at purchase on myparking.cornell.edu; passes expire August 31
fact_check.note: All stated on the page. myparking.cornell.edu purchase page itself was not opened (article admits this); $200/9 = $22 is correct.

fact_check.claim: First-year students ride TCAT free; after first year free unlimited rides after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day Saturday and Sunday
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Sun reported in November 2024 that students who had been riding free at all hours lost that access
fact_check.note: Article reports the mid-October 2024 loss of 24/7 access for non-first-years without a pass; also says pass costs $200 a year.

fact_check.claim: CostLiving: tight $2,190, moderate $3,650, comfortable $5,658; tight tier shared housing $900-$1,100 and minimal dining out; 'CostLiving Engine, September 2026'; cites BLS and City of Ithaca data
fact_check.note: Figures and engine date match. Page says tight needs shared housing ($900-$1,100) and tight grocery and dining spending. Unsupported quotation removed, as asked.

fact_check.claim: CostLiving moderate tier assumes a one-bedroom apartment or small house
fact_check.note: Page gives moderate average housing about $1,972 and one-bedrooms $1,400-$1,700; the phrase 'one-bedroom apartment or small house' was not found in the returned text.

fact_check.claim: CostLiving says TCAT is free for students
fact_check.note: Page says TCAT buses are free for students.

fact_check.claim: NY DPS winter: 600 kWh about $74 a month for supply; 140 therms natural gas about $241 a month, November through March
fact_check.note: Matches the 2026-27 winter outlook. Article correctly notes the figures omit electric delivery charges; the $315 sum is the article's own.

fact_check.claim: EnergySage: Ithaca average about $280 a month on about 1,116 kWh, from residents shopping for solar who may use more
fact_check.note: Matches, including the solar-shopper caveat. Article says 'for electricity and heat'; the EnergySage figure is electricity only, so heat is not covered by that number.

fact_check.claim: Your share of $280-$315 split two to four ways is $70 to $160
Spectrum Internet 500 is $40 a month for one year; standard rates apply after, not stated
fact_check.note: Matches. $10-$20 share is correct arithmetic.

fact_check.claim: Visible base plan $25 a month with taxes and fees included; described as 'one prepaid unlimited plan'
fact_check.note: Page says unlimited data, talk, text and hotspot for $25/mo and 'Taxes and fees included', but does not say the plan is prepaid. The word 'prepaid' (table and Phone paragraph) is unsupported.

fact_check.claim: USDA Low-Cost Food Plan Sept 2026: $63.80 a week (woman 19-50) and $73.30 (man), +20% for a one-person household, 36 weeks gives about $2,960
fact_check.note: The PDF came back as compressed binary; its text could not be read, and the USDA index page returned HTTP 403. The arithmetic checks ((63.80+73.30)/2 x 1.2 x 36 = $2,961; /9 = $329) but the weekly costs were not confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's budget has no phone line
fact_check.note: Listed lines are housing, food, books, personal, transportation only.

beats_top.query: cornell cost of living ithaca student monthly budget
beats_top.why: The search returned Cornell's own aid pages (annual figures only, transportation 'Varies') and aggregators that disagree with each other; none gives a student a monthly line-by-line total with utilities and phone. Our first paragraph answers with a range, and the table shows the sources.
changes: Fix the $2,420 figure in the 'If you are' bullet so it matches the table.
Drop 'prepaid' for the phone plan, or cite a page that says it.
Confirm the USDA weekly figures from a readable USDA page and cite it.

fixes: In the 'If you are... In a newer Collegetown apartment' bullet, change 'near $2,420 with utilities and phone' to 'about $2,520 to $2,620 with utilities and phone' ($1,707 + $330 + $137 + $242 + $0 to $22 bus + $105 to $205 utilities and phone), or say '$2,420 before utilities and phone'.
Remove 'prepaid' from the Phone row of the table and the Phone paragraph; write 'Visible's base plan, $25 a month with taxes and fees included' (source https://www.visible.com/plans/base).
Change 'Electricity and heat' wording so the EnergySage $280 is described as an electricity-only average; keep the DPS gas figure as the heat estimate.
Replace the USDA PDF link with a readable USDA page that lists the Low-Cost Plan weekly costs for ages 19-50 (September 2026), or state that the PDF could not be machine-read.
Remove 'one-bedroom apartment or small house' from the CostLiving moderate-tier description, or say only that the page gives moderate average housing of about $1,972 a month.
